title: Selected TESS CPVs show less sharp-feature shape memory at large sector separations
abstract: We test whether repeated periods in complex periodic variables (CPVs) also imply repeated sharp light-curve shapes. We use published sector 56 to 107 TESS curves for 126 on-target CPVs. We compare harmonics 4 to 12 after a free phase shift and amplitude scale. At separations of one or two sectors, 50 stars have mean shape correlation 0.838. Excess above matched shapes from other CPVs is 0.105, with a 95% star-bootstrap interval of 0.077 to 0.132. At separations of ten or more sectors, 40 stars give excess 0.005 (-0.025 to 0.038). Among 27 stars with both separations, the excess falls by 0.104 (0.067 to 0.141). A control that preserves harmonic power but randomizes harmonic phases gives the same direction. Signal-to-noise cut tests retain the decline. This quantifies loss of sector-averaged shape memory beyond period persistence. It does not measure material survival or identify the opacity source. Source selection, period error, repeated donor curves and uncertain labels limit inference. Original code, aggregate evidence, input hashes and separate-scratch repeat steps are included. External record tables are excluded.

display.caption: Star-weighted sharp-shape agreement across sector intervals. Error bars show 95% star-bootstrap intervals for excess above two controls. These measure waveform memory, not material lifetime.

citations.reason: Uses three verified published products to test sharp-shape memory beyond period persistence.
Campaign luminosity study defines a different prior question; no code or outputs reused.
Earlier evidence for evolving shapes at stable periods; our study adds harmonic controls and population estimates.
